tagline: Where East meets West — domes, minarets, golden light over the Bosphorus.
bestSeason: Apr–May / Sep–Oct (mild, fewer crowds, soft light)

spots.name: Hagia Sophia
spots.bestTime: Early morning (08:00–09:00) before the tour buses arrive
angles: Shoot the exterior from Sultanahmet Square to the northwest — the minarets frame the central dome and the pink-grey walls glow in low side light.
Come back at blue hour: the building is floodlit and the deep blue sky makes the warm stone pop (see photo 2).
Inside, point straight up at the central dome to capture the ring of windows and the gold calligraphy medallions (photo 3). Brace on a railing — it's dim, around 1/30s.
spots.gear: Wide 16mm (24mm equiv) or wider for interiors. Bump ISO to 3200–6400; the interior is much darker than it looks.

spots.name: Blue Mosque
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon to blue hour, when the mosque is lit and the sky deepens
angles: Best vantage is from the gardens between the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia — the fountain and palm trees give you foreground and lead the eye to the six minarets (photo 1).
Get low and shoot the cascading 'wedding-cake' domes slightly off-centre for depth rather than dead-on symmetry.
At sunset / blue hour the sky turns pink-violet behind the silhouetted minarets (photos 2–3) — Velvia's saturation makes this sing.
spots.gear: Tripod for blue hour (1–4s exposures). A polariser cuts glare on the domes and deepens the sky.

spots.name: Galata Tower
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon into sunset — climb the tower ~1 hour before golden hour
angles: Shoot the tower straight on from the small plaza at its base (photo 1) — the conical cap and stone drum fill the frame against blue sky.
Back up into the streets of Karaköy/Galata and let the rooftops and converging buildings frame the tower (photo 2).
At golden hour from across the Golden Horn the whole hillside glows and seagulls circle the tower (photo 3) — pre-focus and shoot bursts to catch a bird in frame.
spots.gear: 35mm (50mm equiv) for the street compression; wide for the rooftop panorama. Tower gets crowded — go at opening.

spots.name: Istanbul Streets
spots.bestTime: Late-afternoon golden light, or evening when İstiklal's lights and crowds come alive
angles: İstiklal Avenue is one long pedestrian river — plant yourself and let people flow past, or shoot from the hip for candid moments (photo 1).
Wait for the nostalgic red tram and frame it head-on down the street; it moves slowly so you can compose and catch passengers leaning out (photo 2).
Look up — the Beyoğlu facades, ornate balconies and wrought-iron street lamps make strong graphic backdrops (photo 3).
Duck into the steep side streets of Karaköy/Galata; converging buildings and a sliver of sky create natural leading lines and frames (photo 4).
spots.gear: A 23mm or 35mm (35/50mm equiv) prime is ideal. Zone-focus around f/8 and keep shutter ≥1/250s to freeze walkers. Classic Neg. gives that punchy-yet-faded documentary street look.

spots.name: Grand Bazaar
spots.bestTime: Mid-morning (10:00–12:00) — shops open, light streams through the skylights
angles: Stand in the middle of an aisle and use the painted vaulted ceiling as a leading line — the arches recede into the distance (photo 1).
Frame a single shopfront or stall packed with colourful goods — hats, lamps, textiles (photo 2). Fujicolor 200's punchy colour suits it.
In the older han courtyards, the worn stone columns and arches make a great wide environmental shot (photo 3); expose for the bright shop lights and let the vaults go moody.
spots.gear: Fast prime (f/2 or wider) for the dim interior; ISO 1600–6400. Keep your bag in front — it's crowded.

spots.name: Bosphorus & Maiden's Tower
spots.nameZh: 博斯普魯斯海峽與少女塔
spots.bestTime: Golden hour from a Bosphorus ferry, or from the Üsküdar / Galata Bridge shore
angles: Maiden's Tower sits mid-strait — shoot it from the Üsküdar shore with the old-city skyline faint behind (photo 1).
Wait for a passing ferry or fishing boat to enter the frame for scale and a sense of movement (photo 2).
From the Galata Bridge, the skyline rises straight from the water (photo 3); the fishermen's rods make a strong repeating foreground.
For the classic panorama, shoot from a rooftop over the Golden Horn at dusk — mosques line the ridge and ferries trail wakes (photo 4). Eterna's muted tones suit the hazy, backlit harbour light.
spots.gear: Telephoto 50–200mm (75–300 equiv) to compress the skyline from the water; a tripod helps at dusk.

spots.name: Basilica Cistern
spots.bestTime: Any time — it's underground and atmospherically lit
angles: Use the endless rows of lit columns reflected in the shallow water for a moody, symmetrical shot (photos 1–2).
The upside-down Medusa-head column base is the must-shoot detail (photo 3).
Brace on the railing for a steady long exposure — it's dark and atmospheric.
spots.gear: Fast wide lens, high ISO (3200–12800). Eterna holds the warm-lit shadows without clipping.

spots.name: Spice Bazaar
spots.bestTime: Late morning when light fills the vaulted hall
angles: Stand centre-aisle and let the painted L-shaped vault recede as a leading line (photos 1–2).
Frame a spice or lokum stall bursting with colour — mounds of saffron, tea and Turkish delight.
Catch shoppers mid-stride under the arches for life and scale.
spots.gear: Fast standard zoom; ISO 1600+. Fujicolor 200's punchy colour suits the spices and lamps.

spots.name: Taksim Square
spots.bestTime: Evening, when the square and İstiklal fill with people and lights
angles: Frame the Republic Monument as the centrepiece of the square (photo 1).
Shoot the wide-open plaza with crowds and the AKM cultural centre as backdrop (photo 2).
Use the square as the gateway to İstiklal Avenue for street-life sequences.
spots.gear: 23–35mm. Classic Neg. for lively, documentary street colour.

tagline: Lunar valleys, cave churches and a sky full of balloons at dawn.
bestSeason: Apr–Jun / Sep–Oct (calm mornings, best balloon-flight odds)

spots.name: Hot-Air Balloons at Sunrise
spots.bestTime: First light — be on a viewpoint (or in a balloon) 20–30 min before sunrise
angles: From a hill in Göreme, shoot wide as dozens of balloons lift together — include foreground rock for depth (photo 1).
Use the rising sun as a backlight and let a single balloon become a silhouette against the glow (photo 1).
If you fly, shoot down onto the striped valleys with other balloons mid-frame for scale (photo 3).
spots.gear: Wide to standard zoom (16–55). Meter for the bright sky and let foreground stay dark; ISO low. Velvia adds punch to the dawn colour.

spots.name: Göreme Open-Air Museum
spots.bestTime: Opening time (08:00) for soft light and fewer crowds
angles: Frame the rock-cut church facades against deep blue sky — the carved doorways read as graphic shapes (photo 1).
Step back for the town-and-valley overview where cave dwellings pepper the hillside (photos 2–3).
Inside the chapels photography is often restricted — respect signs; shoot the exteriors and tunnels instead.
spots.gear: 23–35mm prime. The warm tuff stone loves Kodachrome 64's muted-warm palette.

spots.name: Fairy Chimneys & Rock Valleys
spots.nameZh: 精靈煙囪與奇岩 (帕夏貝/獵人谷)
spots.bestTime: Golden hour, when low light rakes across the rock and brings out texture
angles: Use a path or road as a leading line into the chimney field (photo 2).
Side-light at golden hour makes the eroded cones and 'mushroom' rocks pop in 3D (photos 1, 4).
Climb a ridge for a layered panorama of the striped valleys (photos 3, 5).
spots.gear: Standard to short tele (35–90) to compress the rock layers. A polariser deepens the sky. Velvia for saturated rock tones.

spots.name: Uçhisar Castle
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon to sunset from the castle rock or facing it
angles: Shoot the honeycombed castle rock rising above the village (photos 1–2).
Climb to the top for a 360° panorama over Pigeon Valley at sunset.
In the lanes below, frame an old cart or doorway against the minaret and rock (photo 3).
spots.gear: Wide for the castle mass; 35mm for lanes. Best colour in the last hour of light.

spots.name: Kaymaklı Underground City
spots.bestTime: Any time — it's underground; midday avoids surface heat
angles: Brace against the carved walls for long-ish exposures in the dim tunnels (photo 1).
Use the worn stairways and round 'millstone' doors as compositional anchors.
Include a person for scale in the low passages — it tells the claustrophobic story.
spots.gear: Fast wide lens, high ISO (3200–12800). Eterna's gentle contrast holds the deep shadows without clipping.

tagline: Turkey's monumental capital — Atatürk's mausoleum and an ancient hilltop citadel.

spots.name: Anıtkabir
spots.bestTime: Mid-morning or late afternoon for raking light on the limestone colonnade
angles: Shoot straight down the long ceremonial avenue (Lion Road) so the colonnaded mausoleum sits centred at the end (photos 1–2).
Get low and let the monumental columns tower over the frame against blue sky.
Include the patterned stone plaza as foreground leading lines toward the building (photo 3).
spots.gear: Wide 16mm for the symmetry; a polariser deepens the sky. Velvia gives the pale stone and flags punch.

spots.name: Ankara Castle
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon to sunset from the ramparts over the old town
angles: Climb to the walls for a rooftop panorama over Ankara's old quarter at golden hour.
Frame the weathered towers against the sky; the festival bunting adds colour and lines (photo 1).
In the lanes below, shoot doorways and stone walls for texture-rich street frames.
spots.gear: 23–35mm prime. Classic Neg. suits the warm stone and old-town mood.

tagline: Spiritual heart of the whirling dervishes and Rumi's turquoise-domed shrine.

spots.name: Mevlâna Museum
spots.bestTime: Morning for soft light on the fluted turquoise dome
angles: The fluted turquoise 'Green Dome' is the hero — frame it with the minaret against blue sky (photo 1).
Shoot from the courtyard with people for scale and a sense of pilgrimage.
Inside, photography may be restricted — respect signage and focus on the exterior and courtyard.
spots.gear: Standard zoom. Kodachrome 64's muted warmth balances the vivid dome without over-saturating.

tagline: The largest Seljuk caravanserai on the old Silk Road, a fortress for camel caravans.

spots.name: Sultan Han Caravanserai
spots.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon for side-light on the carved portal
angles: Shoot the monumental carved stone portal straight on — it's the showpiece (photo 1).
Move in close for the intricate muqarnas (stalactite) carving in the doorway (photo 2).
Inside the courtyard, use the arcades and the central kiosk-mosque as leading lines.
spots.gear: Wide for the portal; macro/tele for carving detail. Classic Neg. suits the weathered honey-coloured stone.

tagline: Snow-white travertine terraces and the Roman ruins of Hierapolis above.

spots.name: Pamukkale Travertines
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon to sunset — low light turns the white terraces gold and the pools mirror the sky
angles: Use the stepped pools as repeating foreground curves leading uphill (photos 1–2).
At sunset the white calcium glows warm and the blue water pops — shoot into the light for reflections.
Look for a lone figure on the terraces for scale against the vast white slope.
spots.gear: Wide to standard. A polariser controls glare on the water; ND helps for silky long exposures. Velvia for saturated pools.

spots.name: Hierapolis
spots.bestTime: Golden hour, when the marble ruins warm up
angles: Walk the colonnaded main street and shoot the arch framing the path (photo 1).
The huge Roman theatre is best from the upper tiers looking down across the stage (photo 2).
Combine ruins in the foreground with the white travertines below for a layered story.
spots.gear: Standard zoom; short tele to compress the theatre tiers. Kodachrome 64 flatters the warm stone.

tagline: The grandest classical ruins in the Mediterranean — marble streets and the Library of Celsus.
bestSeason: Apr–Jun / Sep–Oct (early to beat heat & crowds)

spots.name: Library of Celsus
spots.bestTime: Early morning (opening) for soft light and an empty forecourt
angles: Shoot the two-storey facade straight on to celebrate its symmetry (photo 1).
Step to the side and use the marble street as a leading line toward the library.
Include the statues in the niches as detail shots with a short tele.
spots.gear: Wide for the facade; 50mm-equiv for details. Kodachrome 64 renders the warm marble beautifully.

spots.name: Great Theatre
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon as the hillside seats catch warm light
angles: Climb the seating for a sweeping view down the tiers toward the ancient harbour road (photo 1).
Use the curve of the cavea as a strong compositional sweep.
Place people on the steps for scale — the theatre held 25,000.
spots.gear: Wide to capture the scale; a polariser deepens the sky over the pale stone.

tagline: A hillside Greek-era village of white houses, vineyards and fruit wine.

spots.name: Şirince Village
spots.bestTime: Golden hour, when the white houses warm against the green hills
angles: From across the valley, compress the white houses stacked up the green hillside with a short tele (photo 1).
Wander the narrow lanes for doorway, vine and craft-stall detail shots.
Shoot back down an alley with the hills beyond for depth.
spots.gear: 35–90mm to compress the hillside. Kodachrome 64 flatters the warm stone and foliage.

tagline: Breezy Aegean cruise port with a causeway out to Pigeon Island castle.

spots.name: Kuşadası Waterfront
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon to sunset along the promenade
angles: Shoot the palm-lined promenade with the marina and Pigeon Island causeway leading the eye out to sea (photo 1).
At sunset, silhouette the island fortress against the colour over the Aegean.
Use the boats and palms as foreground framing.
spots.gear: Wide to standard. A polariser deepens the sea; Velvia for vivid seaside colour.

tagline: Breezy Aegean port — a beloved clock tower and a century-old cliff elevator.

spots.name: İzmir Clock Tower
spots.bestTime: Sunset to blue hour, when the tower is lit and pigeons fill Konak Square
angles: Shoot the ornate tower against the deep blue dusk sky when it's floodlit (photo 1).
From across Konak Square, catch pigeons taking off with the tower and mosque behind (photo 2).
Get low for a dramatic upward angle of the marble filigree.
spots.gear: 23–35mm. Tripod for blue hour. Classic Neg. gives a lively, slightly retro street look.

spots.name: Asansör
spots.bestTime: Sunset — ride up for the view over the Gulf of İzmir
angles: From the top terrace, shoot the gulf and rooftops at sunset (photo 1).
Frame the historic brick elevator tower against the sky from the street below.
Use the narrow, picturesque Dario Moreno Street as a leading line up to the lift.
spots.gear: Standard zoom. Eterna's gentle tones suit the hazy seaside light.

tagline: The first Ottoman capital, framed by Mount Uludağ — home of the great Ulu Camii.

spots.name: Ulu Camii (Grand Mosque)
spots.bestTime: Midday, when light pours through the upper windows onto the şadırvan fountain
angles: The indoor şadırvan (ablution fountain) under the skylight is unique — shoot it framed by the great arches (photos 1, 3).
Capture the giant black calligraphy panels against the pale walls and 20 domes.
Use the receding arches as symmetrical leading lines down the prayer hall.
spots.gear: Fast wide lens; ISO 1600–6400 indoors. Kodachrome 64 keeps the warm stone natural.

tagline: Palaces and hanok alleys meet neon night markets and futuristic architecture.

spots.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
spots.bestTime: Opening (09:00) for soft light; catch the changing-of-the-guard ceremony mid-morning
angles: Shoot Gyeonghoeru pavilion mirrored in its pond — go early for still water and a clean reflection (photo 1).
Frame the throne hall Geunjeongjeon straight down the stone court with the rank-stones as leading lines (photo 2).
Look up into the painted dancheong eaves and coffered ceilings for rich colour detail (photo 3).
Visitors in rented hanbok add colour — a great foreground subject against the grey stone.
spots.gear: Wide 16mm for the courts; 35mm for hanbok portraits. Kodachrome 64's muted warmth suits the aged wood and paint.

spots.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
spots.bestTime: Early morning or blue hour — quiet lanes, soft light, respectful of residents
angles: Shoot up the sloping Bukchon-ro 11-gil lane with tiled hanok roofs receding and the modern skyline beyond (photo 1).
At blue hour the lantern-lit alleys glow — brace for a steady low-light frame.
Isolate a single hanok gate, wooden door or stone wall for texture (photo 2). Keep noise down — people live here.
spots.gear: 23–35mm prime. Classic Neg. gives the tiles and wood a punchy-yet-faded documentary feel.

spots.name: N Seoul Tower (Namsan)
spots.bestTime: Sunset into blue hour — the city lights come up as the sky still holds colour
angles: Shoot the tower rising from wooded Namsan against clear sky from the plaza below (photo 1).
From the observation deck, capture the endless city at dusk — the golden-to-blue gradient over the skyline (photo 2).
Compress the dense downtown grid with a short tele from the top (photo 3).
The 'love-lock' fences make a colourful foreground for the skyline.
spots.gear: Wide for the tower; 50–200mm to compress the skyline. Tripod for blue hour. Eterna's muted tones suit hazy city light.

spots.name: Myeongdong
spots.bestTime: Evening, when the shopping streets fill with neon, crowds and street-food carts
angles: Shoot down the neon-lit main drag with signboards stacked up both sides (photo 1).
Use the street-food carts' warm light and steam as a foreground against the cool neon.
Catch motion — buses and crowds — with a slower shutter for energy.
spots.gear: Fast 23–35mm, ISO 3200–6400. Cinestill 800T recipe nails the tungsten-neon night-cinema glow.

spots.name: Gwangjang Market
spots.bestTime: Late morning to evening, when the food alleys are busiest
angles: Shoot down the covered food alley with hanging flags and stall lights as a bright leading line (photos 1–2).
Frame a bindaetteok or gimbap stall mid-action — sizzling pans and colourful banchan.
Grab candid diners at the counters; ask before close portraits.
spots.gear: Fast standard zoom, ISO 1600+. Fujicolor 200's punchy colour loves the food and flags.

spots.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
spots.bestTime: Blue hour to night, when the curving facade is lit and LED roses glow
angles: Use the flowing aluminium curves of Zaha Hadid's building as sweeping abstract lines (photo 1).
At night, long-expose the adjacent road for light trails against the silver facade.
Get low and let the ramps and seams lead the eye through the frame.
spots.gear: Wide for the curves; tripod + ND for light trails. Vintage Cinema recipe suits the moody metallic night look.
